EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows a very strong band at 721 cm⁻¹ that is characteristic of the C–H out-of-plane bend of a monosubstituted benzene ring. Peaks at 1567 and 1590 cm⁻¹ fit the usual aromatic C=C stretches. The single N–H stretching band appears at 3132 cm⁻¹, consistent with a secondary amine (one N–H). Bands at 1095 and 1040 cm⁻¹ are in the typical C–N stretching region, and aliphatic C–H stretches (2913, 2862 cm⁻¹) and deformations (1449, 1200 cm⁻¹) match a small alkyl chain. Among the candidates, only CNCc1ccccc1 (1) contains a monosubstituted phenyl plus a secondary amine and no halogen/extra substituents that would add distinctive bands. Therefore candidate 1 best matches the observed Raman features.
